name: Meeting Ops
how: Catches the call-end webhook and pulls the transcript via Zoom/Otter's API, writes a structured summary into the meeting's Notion page, creates action-item tasks in Linear with owners, and drafts the follow-up email in Gmail for one-tap send.
use: A client call ends at 3pm; by 3:05 the notes are filed, tasks are assigned, and the follow-up email is waiting in drafts.

name: Email Copilot
how: Reads new priority threads and your sent-mail history through the Gmail API to learn your voice, then writes draft replies straight back into your Gmail drafts folder — you just review and send.
use: You open Gmail to find every important email already has a reply drafted in your tone.

name: Community Manager
how: Every hour it fetches new comments via the YouTube Data API, drafts replies in your voice, flags the ones needing a human, and logs recurring questions to Notion as future video ideas.
use: Your top comments get thoughtful replies within the hour, and FAQs quietly become your next script.

name: Topic Backlog Manager
how: Continuously pulls new papers from arXiv/HuggingFace and trend signals via web search, scores each against search demand, and maintains a ranked video-idea database in Notion that it re-orders every week.
use: You never wonder what to film next — the top of your Notion backlog is always the best bet.

name: Researched Script Builder
how: When a topic is promoted, it gathers primary sources via web + arXiv, extracts cited facts, drafts a retention-structured script, and saves it with a full source list to Notion.
use: Promote a topic in the morning; a sourced, fact-checked script is sitting in Notion by lunch.

name: Publish Prep
how: On an unlisted upload it queries the YouTube API to verify thumbnail, cards and end screen are set, generates keyword-ranked titles and a description via web search, and blocks publish if anything is missing.
use: Upload a draft and the agent won't let it go public until every metadata box is checked.

name: Content Distributor
how: When new content publishes, it drafts platform-native posts (LinkedIn, X thread, newsletter blurb) and queues each into its scheduler at your best-performing time slot.
use: One video upload automatically becomes four scheduled posts across your channels.

name: Channel Intelligence
how: Every Monday it pulls retention curves, CTR and traffic-source data through the YouTube Analytics API, identifies what's actually growing, and writes recommendations back into the topic backlog.
use: Monday morning you learn which videos are winning and exactly what to make more of.

name: Invoice Creator
how: When a project milestone is marked billable in Notion, it creates and sends a real invoice via the Stripe API and writes the invoice ID back to Notion for tracking.
use: Mark a milestone done and the client gets a professional invoice minutes later.

name: Cash Flow Command
how: Weekly it reads Stripe invoices and Notion expenses to project your forward cash position, and on overdue-invoice events sends polite payment-reminder emails via Gmail.
use: Every Friday you see next month's cash position and overdue clients get auto-nudged.

name: Expense Ledger
how: Watches Gmail for receipt emails and syncs bank transactions via Plaid, categorizes and matches them to each other, then writes a clean ledger to your accounting tool and flags anything unmatched.
use: Receipts and card charges reconcile themselves into a categorized ledger each week.

name: Tax Prep Assistant
how: Quarterly it pulls receipts from Gmail and financial records from Notion, organizes everything by tax category, and outputs a clean handoff package.
use: At quarter-end your books are sorted for the accountant with zero scramble.

name: GitHub PR Warden
how: On PR events and a 9am sweep it queries the GitHub API for open PRs, flags the ones that are stale or waiting on you, and nudges you so review debt doesn't pile up.
use: Stale pull requests get surfaced daily instead of rotting for a week.

name: Issue Triage Agent
how: When a new issue is opened it reads it via the GitHub API, applies labels and priority, and assigns it or creates a matching task in Linear.
use: Every new issue is labeled, prioritized, and assigned the moment it lands.

name: Weekly Review
how: Every Friday it queries Linear, GitHub and Notion for what shipped and what slipped, then writes a grounded review doc from the real activity.
use: Friday 5pm you get a factual snapshot of the week — wins, slips, and what Monday looks like.

name: Cold Outreach Sequencer
how: On a new CRM lead it enriches from LinkedIn/Clearbit, writes a personalized email grounded in their recent activity, sends via the CRM, and runs a 3-step follow-up that stops the instant they reply.
use: Add a lead and a personalized outreach sequence runs itself until they respond.

name: Meeting Prep + Dossier
how: 60 minutes before an external meeting it reads the Calendar event, pulls the attendee's LinkedIn and recent company news, your Gmail history with them, and any CRM notes into a one-page brief.
use: You walk into every call already knowing who you're meeting and what was last said.

name: Competitor Radar
how: Continuously monitors named competitors and topics via web and news sources, and only alerts you when something actually changes — a launch, a price move, a funding round.
use: You hear about a rival's launch the moment it happens, not a week later.

name: Contract & NDA Guard
how: When a contract arrives via Gmail or Drive it reads the document, flags risky clauses in plain English, and routes an approve / escalate / reject recommendation.
use: A contract lands and you instantly know which clause needs a second look.

name: Renewal Sentinel
how: Tracks insurance, business-registration and license renewal dates and alerts you well ahead of each lapse.
use: You're warned 90 days before insurance renews, so coverage never lapses.

name: Deep Research Agent
how: On demand it orchestrates multiple sequential web searches, cross-references the sources, and synthesizes a cited report.
use: Ask a hard question and get a sourced, multi-source report instead of a shallow answer.

name: Read-It-Later Digester
how: Processes your Pocket/Readwise saves and podcast RSS feeds, summarizes each, extracts standout quotes, and files structured notes to Notion while reordering your queue by your current goals.
use: Everything you saved but never read comes back as summarized, searchable notes.

name: Document Studio
how: Pulls real project data from CRM/Notion and your past winning docs as templates to generate proposals, SOWs and agreements, then files them to Drive and sends where relevant.
use: Generate a client-ready proposal grounded in real project data in minutes.

name: Onboarding Orchestrator
how: On a new hire or contractor it sends the contract via e-sign, provisions tool and GitHub access, creates the onboarding task checklist in Notion, and schedules the kickoff.
use: A new contractor is signed, provisioned, and scheduled without you lifting a finger.
